Once the pity period ends, it's just a gacha game, designed to demoralise you into wasting money or wasting time. There are invisible caps on what you're able to get as a freeloader, the careers quickly turn into a grind, the dailies are honestly skippable unless there's an event going on, shit just drags - around 20 to 30 minutes for a single run, even if you're on full autoskip.

If you like the anime horse girls, it's okay. It's a very good franchise which treats historical horses and their careers with great respect and attention to detail. You can enjoy that away from the game though, by watching the anime series, in particular the movies and Cinderella Gray are probably some of the best sports Chinese cartoons in a long time. If you think this will be the one gacha that *clicks* for you - it probably won't, unless you're already a gacha addict.

If you already gave it a go, don't blame yourself for dropping it. If you're thinking of giving it a go, I suggest you don't.

Whales VS F2P

F2P
Playing F2P is totally possible if you just enjoy the story and the lore of the horses.
The game gives lots of free pulls over time since we are on an accelerated path compared to the JP version of the game.
Its recommended that you pull on cards when you first start out and pull on horses when you have some extra carrots.
There are tons of guides and even a banner page online tracking the upcoming banners and more if you need some more F2P tips. Being a F2P player IS DOABLE with some luck and just playing for dailies.

Whales
Well, you know... Whales can obviously get passed the game quicker to the end game comp CM scene.
But without the knowledge I have seen some whales lose during some competitive CM's.
Pull on what you want I guess.

Overall

I was never a gacha player, I only played ZZZ but it really wasn't my thing. But Umamusume has tons of horses with different personalities, you can pick your favorite and just enjoy the game instead of trying to be competitive .
Lock in, have fun, don't wasted all your carrots and always roll on 99%, gamblers always quit before hitting big.
Just be scared of the woman with a needle.

250 pulls. Only one copy of SSR Kitasan Black to show for it.

Yes, I know this is a Cygames game and technically it has a “pity” system — the infamous spark at 200 pulls. But let’s be real: that’s not a real pity system by today’s standards. You can easily go 200 pulls without getting any banner SSRs, and if you're pulling for support cards, one copy isn't nearly enough. You need several just to make them viable.

Other modern gachas have caught up: soft pities, guaranteed SSRs at intervals, dupe systems that respect your investment. Meanwhile, this game still runs on outdated, brutal RNG that punishes even the most dedicated players.

It feels like a system designed to frustrate you into spending, and I’m just tired of it. Gacha games can be fun, but this? This is just exhausting.

I’m out.

I've waited 4 and a half years for this game to release globally, and it was well worth the wait! You can easily tell the devs put in all their effort to make the global servers as successful as they already did with the Japanese servers.

While the game is addicting as hell, training can be kinda frustrating and at times discouraging, but it comes with the territory lol. Just keep playing the game, prioritize pulling for SSR support cards that'll help make training Umas a lot smoother, only pull Umas if they're your waifus, and just simply have a fun time. You'll get your good endings and B rank (or better) Umas in no time!

Thank you Cygames for bringing the game to us outside of Japan! I'm sorry Princess Connect (RIP global server </3) you basically had to be the ultimate sacrifice for this to happen. Your EOS wasn't in vain.

Anyway, PLAY THE GREATEST GACHA GAME OF ALL TIME.

Just want to say, if you see any comments about "Not being able to win within 2-4 times of doing the career and you need 3 star horses", that is flat out a skill issue, just make sure to get Fine Motion or Super Creek, whichever you like the most, and you can easily do a full run no issues with SRs. The game is fresh, so not many people have super built friend units yet, as well as you as the player, so its essentially working your way up to get full complete runs. You can add people BEFORE you start training and have good friend helpers to start out with, that will make the world's difference. Also every character is viable, sometimes more than others but what game doesn't have that, so train whoever you want.
